And the Ministry of Science is the go-between between the budget on the one hand and this whole scientific research community and system on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, as you told us yesterday, in addition to your academic involvements, you have been a rather prominent, in fact, social and political activist, I believe you said, over the past 20 years; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct in part. I mentioned that I was very active in social life, not in political life. I was very active in the civil society of the Republic of Croatia, mostly in the field of social cohesion and human rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say, sir, that during that time, during those 20 years of activism you have been often identified as someone on the -- on the right wing of the political spectrum?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would depend on how talk to, because there were various stereotypes that were attributed to me, but there are other opinions, too, because, unfortunately, in Croatia politics permeates everything. Everything is seen through politics, and people only look at things in black and white, right or left. It's part of our Communist heritage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You are --

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. You are also a member or perhaps an officer, you can assist us, please, but you're active in the Croatian homeland war volumes association? I thinks' sometimes called the UHDDR?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have one U too many here. It's a NGO. All those are NGOs, so it's part of the civil society. These are associations that proceeded from the Croatian homeland war, and if you look at this page -- could I please have the Croatian version on the monitor at the same place. I would like you to move on in the Croatian version so that we have the two versions at the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may help. If there is no document in binder, maybe I can borrow my copy of the curriculum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe it should be in the first binder. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you go behind the English -- okay?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll also try to assist you on the screen if we can, but you should always have the document as well. Yes. All right. Well, looking under "Membership," sir, I think that is what you were referring the courtroom's attention to. If you look under "Membership," you mention a number of organisations there. Lest I be misunderstood, I'm not questioning at the moment the value or validity of any sort of veterans' association, but in the particular political circumstances of Croatia, and your comments a moment ago that everything in Croatia is political, these are considered as right-wing organisations; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That association cannot be considered a right-wing association, not based on its statutory provisions. And as regards my activism in those associations, it is a well-known fact in Croatia that I advocated the interest of the victims of the Croatian homeland war, and that includes the volunteers, and that I have been in fierce conflict with the government structures in the Republic of Croatia, including the current government, the HDZ government, because of its discrimination of the participants in the Croatian homeland war. You can see a number of speeches that I made and other public appearances which are socially in tone. So if you speak about me as a person that has links with the right-wing end of the political spectrum has nothing to do with my social background, my family background, my active -- activism, my positions, and my values that I espouse in my public appearances, and it has nothing to do with the value judgements or the assessments, evaluations of my scientific work which is based on the humanist paradigm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me go back for a moment to the institute where you worked with Mr. Sakic. In fact, you told us Mr. Sakic, as I understood your testimony, is the head of the institute. How long have the two of you worked together at that institute?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is one of the founders of the institute, in 1991. I have been working in the institute since 1997, but I worked with the institute on a number of projects that had to do with the Croatian homeland war. I was not a full-time staff member but as an external associate, and there is a large number of external associates who work on those projects in the institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have the two of you, other than this case, and we'll come at some point to the work you've done on this case and perhaps the work that Mr. Sakic has done, but putting that to the side for the moment, apart from this case, have you and Mr. Sakic worked closely together before? Have you co-published any materials? Are the two of you close colleagues?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would depend on the projects. In the institute, the Ministry of Science has approved various multi-disciplinary projects because the institute employs sociologists, demographers, psychologists, economists, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you just answer my question, please. My question was really not to ask you about the structure of the institute. But the two of you, Mr. Sakic, have you worked together closely through the years and co-published materials and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked on some projects just as I had on -- with some other scholars on projects that were either carried out within the institute or outside of the institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And one last background question, if you will, sir, before moving forward. During the time that you were at IPD in the Croatian Ministry of Defence, did your time there ever overlap with Mr. Zuzul?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning, there were seven or eight founders of the IPD.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was Mr. Zuzul --

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And one of them was Mr. Zuzul. Miroslav Tudjman was also among them, Ivan Tolj, Dr. Knezovic, Rogic, Marinko Lozancic. I may have missed someone because it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. But at least three of the founders we now know were Mr. Zuzul, who has previously testified in this case; Mr. Sakic, who is going to testify in this case; and Miroslav Tudjman, who is the son of President Franjo Tudjman; correct? Those were three of the several founders of the IPD.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Sakic was not among the founders of the IPD.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. That was the institute. I stand corrected. You're right, sir. Mr. Zuzul and Mr. Tudjman were among the founders; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP JURCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm mindful of the efficient use of time, but I'm about to start another topic that I'm not going to be able to finish in the next four minutes. If we might stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're absolutely right. It's best to continue tomorrow if you have a new topic to address. Let me tell you that you've already used up 24 minutes. For some kind of reason which I do not know, we have to sit in room number I, in Courtroom I. Courtroom III will be used by the Popovic case. I don't know why they've been sent to Courtroom I, but now the Judges are going to have to lug their binders, their heavy binders over the court. Fortunately, we'll get some help, I hope so anyway, otherwise we'll strain our backs. We'll be very careful anyway lugging all that. So we will meet tomorrow at 9.00 in Courtroom I. Professor, let me renew what I already told you. We now have confirmation that you are an eminent leader. Please do not contact the media. We've already told you so and I repeat. I repeat this. I wish you all a pleasant afternoon and we resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
